title: Arranging records for Danny White
summary: Writing horn backgrounds from records on a borrowed player.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It was in the early 60s? Yeah. Must be in the early 60s.
I Want a Little Girl to Da Da Da. I think that's it. Want a Little Girl to Love A Lot? Yeah.

I think that's T-Bone Walker. I Want a Little Girl, that's what the name of the song. Yeah but Ray was doing it. Yeah Ray was doing it. I think T-Bone, I remember you the first one did it. Yeah but I Want a Little Girl.
Well the guy used to play that a lot on the joke box, you know, and he asked Danny, could we do that, you know.

Yeah. I want a Little Girl to Love A Lot. Yeah. He said, man, see Danny bent on me, but he didn't, from the neighborhood, but he didn't know that I had the knowledge about music that I did, you know. He told me, he said, man I heard you can arrange. I said, yeah, he said, can you write this, the background for this? I said, yeah, I can write it. I said, but you got to bring me a record player, because I ain't got any player on where I live at. I ain't no record player. So he brought his record player over and he brought the four to five, you know. And I wrote it out, you know. On the staff music. I wrote it off the Cold Hill's record and wrote it on out for horns. We didn't have but two horns then. They had Hulk and Ernest Highlands, because Teddy hadn't got there. He had Teddy Riley. So I voiced it for two horns and the rest. And man, it come out beautiful. And we started playing with man. And so ever since then he used to bring me a record, like two, three, four weeks. And what did he do?
He'd come to my place I lived by myself.

And I said, hey, this record player there, and he'd bring the 45, or the album or whatever. And what I'd have to do, I'd have to, sometimes like a Jack Wilson song or something, it'd be too high or something, and I'd put it in his key. Yeah, I'd put it in the key, come for him to sing. And I'd arrange it. And it'd always come out fine, you know. And man, we got so popular. But them first few rehearsals had real problems, because they wasn't up on their reading, they hadn't read in so long. And then after the more they read, it come back to them. And so man, one time we was playing at the club saying, we got in a big fight with them white boys around there, you know. We got in a fight and so we lost a job. The man got mad and fired us. But they had another man out there at the Club Safari.
